label: absolute-time window t=7-10 in long sequences (around <DEL> for L=8-9), gated by sequence content
explanation: A timing unit tied to absolute step: never active for t<5. Almost all activity falls in t=7-10, and L=9 holds 65% of the mass. In long sequences it fires on the last 1-2 original tokens, the <DEL> step (41% of mass, 4.6% rate) and the first 1-2 copy outputs. Within that window it fires on only about 7% of steps. Which sequences light up depends on content, mainly the first original token (x, f, e, 0, r give 2-4x lift; first_tok=x gives the largest activations). Restricting the window to those first tokens raises precision to about 22% but drops recall to 37%. It does not fire in short sequences (L<=5), at the start of a sequence, or in the middle of the copy phase. There is a small second bump at the last copy steps (t=16-17) of L=9.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: x, f, e, 0, 1, o; least: k, v, w, u) and the current input token, by phase (copy phase: f, r, j, e; input phase: p, v, d, k; delimiter step: <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: L=9, t=7, t=8.
